rationale: D1 of the growth-clock spec for inverse flames, data-informed (not zero-shot). The published growth law does not describe the lean inverse flames (it gives them minutes; they last seconds), so their end is the second clock of the forward, an oscillation and quench clock in the conditions that keeps the self-extinction law of the second generation's D1. The growth clock is switched off: with its published constants it also takes air-injected flames that were still burning at the 66 s stop. What is new against the second generation: the burner limit is a heating law in the total burner flow and the flame size, written from the peak burner temperatures of the train flames (a post-run fact used to write the law, never an input), under which a lean flame cannot reach the limit; the weak class needs both a low adiabatic temperature and a lean ambient; the 66 s script stop is one window from 63 to 67 s at the frequency sessions used it, and stops seen in one session are a background rate at the pooled count. Every number typed by the author; no fit, no search; nothing chosen from validation.
